verdict.rationale: Chronicle's core product is a sandbox for agent testing. Agents read and write simulated twins of vendor APIs, writes stick only inside the twin, reset restores the original seed, and each trial gets fresh twins so nothing carries over. The vendor also says it turns production data into separate staging environments, so tests do not touch the live systems. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the isolation, explicit documentation that twins can never reach real production endpoints.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Simulated services that your agent can read and write through the vendor's API.
Your agent talks to it exactly as it would talk to the real service. Writes stick, and Chronicle records every request and every changed record.
Reset throws away runtime changes and restores the original seed.
every trial gets its own fresh twins built from the saved world... nothing one trial does affects the next.
Turn your production data into staging environments for AI agent testing and validation.
